title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were not designed to handle the specific conditions they encountered during Fourth of July festivities in San Francisco. The cars became stranded when severe traffic congestion caused by fireworks celebrations and unplanned road closures drained their batteries faster than anticipated. At least a dozen vehicles required roadside assistance, with at least one needing removal by flatbed truck.

This is a failure of deployment scope. The vehicles were operating in urban conditions that fell outside their tested or intended operating envelope: extreme traffic density, extended periods of gridlock, and the secondary effects of a major public event. Catching this would have required either restricting service during foreseeable high-congestion events, pre-positioning charging infrastructure, or testing battery resilience under the specific load patterns of holiday traffic. It is not established whether Waymo had predicted this scenario or what constraints, if any, were placed on the system during the event.

A separate fire incident, in which a Waymo vehicle drove over fireworks, shows a different problem: the system's sensors and decision-making encountered an unusual hazard in the environment and did not avoid it. No injuries resulted, but this suggests gaps in how the vehicle perceives and responds to debris and fire hazards on the road.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. The driverless cars, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, had their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion caused by major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Video verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary vehicles lined up on streets, with at least one requiring a flatbed truck for removal. Waymo stated its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and indicated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events.

The incident frustrated motorists who experienced extended delays. One resident reported spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic and noted people were yelling at the Waymo vehicles because they had no drivers. Additionally, a Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set off, though no injuries were reported. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the traffic situation with stakeholders to improve future post-fireworks experiences in the city.
